title_en: Panama Yifa Shipping Company v. Zhong Xiaoyuan et al. — retrial of dispute over compensation for damages from vessel collision

full_text_en:
**Panama Yifa Shipping Company v. Zhong Xiaoyuan et al. — Retrial of Dispute over Vessel Collision Damage Compensation**

**Retrial Applicant (Appellant in the Original Trial and Defendant at First Instance):** Panama Yifa Shipping Company.

**Legal Representative:** Zhu Keli, Director of the Company.

**Other Party (Appellee in the Original Trial and Plaintiff at First Instance):** Zhong Xiaoyuan, male, owner of fishing vessel "Shanwei 12138."

**Other Party (Appellee in the Original Trial and Plaintiff at First Instance):** Anti-Smuggling Office of Zhuhai Municipal Government, Guangdong Province.

**Legal Representative:** Lai Huabao, Director of the Office.

**Other Parties (Appellees in the Original Trial and Plaintiffs at First Instance):** Su Xianggao, Su Qirong, Li Xing, Chen Hua, Liu Yaoxiong — all relatives of the deceased victims of the collision.

**Other Parties (Appellees in the Original Trial and Plaintiffs at First Instance):** Zhong Wu, Zhong Muhuo, Su Zuwang, Su Wang, Su Hua, Xu Peng, Zhong Caibao, Zhong Jiarong, Zhong Jiazhong, Lu Zhihua, Cai Ji, Liu Guobao, Liang Fumin, Mao Xiangwu, and 14 others — all survivors from the collided vessel.

The retrial applicant, Panama Yifa Shipping Company (hereinafter referred to as Yifa Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment that had become legally effective of the Guangdong High People's Court, filed a petition for retrial with the Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China regarding a dispute over damages for vessel collision with the other parties including Zhong Xiaoyuan.

**Facts Found by the Supreme People's Court upon Retrial:**

The vessel involved, "TRADE EXPANSION" (the "Yifa" vessel), is a Panamanian-flagged container freighter owned by the retrial applicant Yifa Company, measuring 163.03 meters in length, 22.93 meters in breadth, and 11.63 meters in depth, with a gross tonnage of 11,825 tons. At 0219 hours on November 25, 1992, the vessel departed from Hong Kong bound for Zhangjiagang.

The collided vessel involved, "Shanwei 12138," was a steel-hulled trawler with a gross tonnage of 155 tons, measuring 29 meters in length, 6.6 meters in breadth, and 3.7 meters in depth. On June 4, 1992, it was registered as a fishing vessel with the Shanwei Fishing Port Superintendency in China, with the owner being the other party Zhong Xiaoyuan. Thereafter, there was no registered change of the vessel's name or use. On November 24, 1992, the vessel was requisitioned by the other party, the Anti-Smuggling Office of Zhuhai Municipal Government, Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Smuggling Office). According to the Anti-Smuggling Office, they renamed "Shanwei 12138" as "Gongbian 001" and departed from Zhuhai Xiangzhou Port to participate in maritime anti-smuggling operations. At the time, there were 14 fishermen, 4 armed police soldiers, 2 assistant anti-smuggling personnel, and 1 female family member accompanying them, totaling 21 persons on board. The testimony of the fishermen and armed police soldiers on board confirmed that the vessel did not display a nameplate reading "Gongbian 001" from the time of departure until its sinking.

According to the fishermen on board "Shanwei 12138": At approximately 0300 hours on November 25, 1992, "Shanwei 12138" arrived in the waters near Dangan Island. At around 0500 hours, the vessel's position was determined using a satellite navigation positioning device (approximate position) as 22°08' N, 114°31' E. Thereafter, a vessel was sighted approaching from the port side, showing two white lights (one forward low, one aft high), a starboard side light, and several pale yellow lights. On radar, a relatively large echo was observed moving eastward. "Shanwei 12138" then changed course to north-northwest to intercept and inspect the vessel, simultaneously switching on its searchlight, warning light, and illumination lights, continuously sounding short blasts on its whistle, and directing the searchlight toward the bridge area of the approaching vessel. When the searchlight shone on the deck, containers were visible on deck, the hull was blackish-gray, and the bridge was white. At the instant when "Shanwei 12138" was crossing the bow of the approaching vessel, the latter turned to port, and the port side of its bow struck the port side engine room area of "Shanwei 12138." "Shanwei 12138" immediately stopped its engine, but its bow swung sharply to port, again striking the port side of the approaching vessel and scraping along its side toward the stern. At the same time, the struck area was damaged, the engine room flooded heavily, the stern sank, and the bow gradually rose. Shortly after the vessel disengaged from the other vessel, it sank. All persons on board "Shanwei 12138" fell into the water along with the vessel. The offending vessel did not provide assistance to the persons in the water and continued sailing eastward.

On December 28, 1992, a certain naval observation and communication station of the People's Liberation Army Navy (hereinafter referred to as the Observation Station) prepared and provided to the Guangzhou Harbor Superintendency a document titled "Detection and Reporting Materials on Maritime Vessels" (hereinafter referred to as the "Detection Materials"), which stated: At 0513 hours on November 25, 1992, the radar echo of a public security vessel with serial number 036 merged with the echo of a foreign merchant vessel with serial number 847 at a position of 22°09'.9 N, 114°31'.5 E. At 0520 hours, the echo of serial number 036 disappeared at a bearing of 065° and a distance of 14 nautical miles from the Observation Station. In the Detection Materials, apart from the foreign merchant vessel with serial number 847 sailing eastward, there were records of the positions of seven other merchant vessels sailing westward into the Dangan水道 or into Hong Kong, but no records of other vessels departing from Hong Kong and sailing eastward. On February 10, 1993, the duty observer of the Observation Station on November 25 testified to the Guangzhou Harbor Superintendency: "Before and after the collision, there were several other vessels in the waters near Dangan Island. On radar, the other vessels observed were all entering Hong Kong or sailing westward. The only vessel sailing eastward was the foreign merchant vessel that sank the public security vessel."

According to the radar observation records of the Vessel Traffic Centre (VTC) of the Hong Kong Marine Department from 0416 to 0800 hours on November 25, 1992, on that day, vessels departing from the Hong Kong水道 and sailing eastward included, in addition to the "TRADE EXPANSION" (the "Yifa" vessel) owned by the retrial applicant Yifa Company (with VTC radar tracking code W448), another container freighter "BARZAN" (with tracking code W500).

The "BARZAN" is a Qatari-flagged container freighter, registered port of Doha, measuring 183.2 meters in length, with a gross tonnage of 20,526 tons. The vessel departed from Hong Kong at 0314 hours on November 25, 1992, bound for Kaohsiung. VTC radar tracking records: At 0500.6 hours, W500's position was 22°10'.810 N, 114°26'.725 E, heading 101°, speed 16 knots. Between 0514 and 0530 hours, the vessel transited the area where the maritime incident occurred. During this period, at 0518.6 hours, the position was 22°09'.909 N, 114°31'.784 E, heading 102°, speed 16.1 knots; at 0520.6 hours, position 22°09'.823 N, 114°32'.332 E, thereafter the heading remained generally around 103°, actual speed approximately 16.1 knots; at 0526.6 hours, position 22°09'.667 N, 114°33'.994 E, the vessel altered course to port to heading 061°, a change of over 40°, actual speed reduced to 13.3 knots; after 0528.6 hours, it gradually returned to its original heading, and speed recovered to over 15 knots.

On November 26, 1992, the master of "BARZAN" submitted a "Marine Accident Report" to Kaohsiung Port, stating: "At 0525 hours on November 25, my chief officer sighted a small vessel very close to the bow, switched the autopilot to hand steering and turned the wheel. The small vessel passed close along my vessel's port side. At that time, local time was 0527 hours on November 25, and my vessel's position was 22°09'.8 N, 114°34'.5 E. The master felt the vessel vibrate and arrived on the bridge at 0530 hours, observing the small vessel at the port quarter position."

Of the 21 persons who fell into the water from "Shanwei 12138," 15 were rescued by a U.S. Navy vessel between 0720 and 0745 hours on November 25, while 5 died and 1 was declared dead. The position where the U.S. Navy vessel rescued the persons in the water was 22°09'.3 N, 114°33'.1 E.

On the same day, between 0850 and 1945 hours, the British Navy vessel "PEACOCK" participated in search and rescue operations in the accident area. The vessel searched against the direction of drift of floating debris from the sunken vessel. At 1551 hours, following a diesel slick on the surface, it located the source of continuously fresh diesel leakage. Using an echo sounder, it detected a new sunken vessel, and determined the position of the sunken vessel using the Global Positioning System (GPS) as 22°09'.4 N, 114°34'.1 E. Subsequently, after diving inspections and positioning by Hong Kong Wesson Marine Engineering Co., Ltd. and Hong Kong Global Geophysical & Geological Survey Co., Ltd., the position of the sunken vessel was fixed at 22°09'.484 N, 114°34'.051 E.

On November 25, 1992, in the area of the maritime incident, morning civil twilight began at 0617 hours, sunrise at 0641 hours, and moonrise at 0719 hours (the previous day's moonset was at 1729 hours). At the time of the incident, it was a moonless night. The wind was northerly, force 2-3. Low tide occurred at 0440 hours, with a slack water period of approximately 30 minutes; high tide at 1140 hours, slack water period approximately 50 minutes. Maximum flood current velocity was 0.6-0.8 knots, winter current generally 0.5-0.6 knots, direction southwest.

On November 30, 1992, the "Yifa" vessel arrived at Zhangjiagang. From December 1 to 5, the Zhangjiagang Harbor Superintendency conducted a maritime investigation of the vessel, photographing its port side from bow to stern, and prepared a scene inspection record dated December 2, 1992. The record stated: On the port side of the "Yifa" vessel, from behind the forward shoulder to the accommodation ladder, over a length of approximately 100 meters, there were intermittent scraping marks pointing toward the stern, particularly evident in the mid-body area and aft. In particular, a scraping mark approximately 7-8 meters long, located 3.5 to 5.4 meters above the waterline in the mid-body area, showed significant damage to the paint film, revealing layers of gray, yellow, and red paint from the surface inward. A black linear scraping mark 0.9 meters above the water surface started slightly aft of the mid-body and disappeared near the accommodation ladder. The Zhangjiagang Harbor Superintendency collected two paint film samples from the damaged paint area and an undamaged area of the "Yifa" vessel. On January 9, 1993, the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau conducted infrared spectroscopy and infrared microscopy tests on these two paint film samples. The control paint sample was provided by Zhong Xiaoyuan, the owner of "Shanwei 12138." The test data showed that some corresponding peak values differed by more than 50 wavenumbers. The test conclusion stated: The paint extracted from the scraping marks on the "Yifa" vessel contained components identical to those in the control paint sample.

During the retrial, the Supreme People's Court commissioned five maritime experts from the Navigation College of Dalian Maritime University to conduct a technical appraisal of the collision facts in this case. The "Technical Appraisal Report" concluded: Based on the wind and current conditions at the time, it could be inferred that the position of the sunken vessel should be to the northeast of the position where the persons in the water were rescued. The position where the persons were rescued and the position where the "PEACOCK" vessel discovered the sunken vessel continuously emitting fresh diesel were consistent with the wind and current conditions at the time. Considering the statements of several persons regarding visibility, the visibility distance at the time was approximately 5 nautical miles. From the time the personnel of "Shanwei 12138" saw the lights of the large vessel (after approximately 0500 hours) to the time of collision, the vessel would have sailed for about 20 to 18 minutes; therefore, the collision time should not have been 0513 hours but rather later. The "Yifa" vessel's heading did not change between 0510 and 0516 hours, which was inconsistent with the fishermen's statement that the offending vessel suddenly turned to port at the time of collision. If the "Yifa" vessel had collided with "Shanwei 12138," the crew members in the water would have been able to see a large vessel (the "BARZAN") passing near them (within less than 185 meters), but none of the persons in the water stated that they saw another large vessel passing. If the "Yifa" vessel had collided with "Shanwei 12138" at 22°09'.9 N, 114°31'.5 E, based on the maneuvering of "Shanwei 12138," its residual speed, its rapid sinking after collision, and the wind and current conditions, the sunken vessel should have been located to the southwest of the collision position; "Shanwei 12138" could not have drifted 2.4 nautical miles against the current to its present position. Therefore, the collision position could not have been 22°09'.9 N, 114°31'.5 E. The "Yifa" vessel was sailing at a speed of 14-15 knots. If it had collided with "Shanwei 12138," there should have been obvious indentation or damage to the port side of its bow, but the port side of the "Yifa" bow was undamaged. The paint scraping marks on the port side of the "Yifa" vessel did not quite match the two scraping marks that would have been caused by the port gunwale and the upper port side of the wheelhouse of "Shanwei 12138." The Hong Kong VTC record of W500 (i.e., "BARZAN") showed a significant turn to port while transiting the accident area, consistent with the statements of the crew of "Shanwei 12138," and this was also confirmed by the master's Marine Accident Report of "BARZAN." The Marine Accident Report stated that the position of the incident was to the northeast of the sunken vessel's position, consistent with the objective law that after collision, the vessel drifted downwind and down-current. "BARZAN" transited the area later than the "Yifa" vessel, which was consistent with the fact that the persons from "Shanwei 12138" did not see a large vessel passing nearby for a period after falling into the water. The appraisal conclusion: 1. The evidence is insufficient to establish that the "Yifa" vessel was the offending vessel that collided with "Shanwei 12138." 2. The possibility that "BARZAN" might have been the offending vessel that collided with "Shanwei 12138" cannot be ruled out.

Following this vessel collision incident, the other parties filed lawsuits with the Guangzhou Maritime Court seeking damages. Among them, Zhong Xiaoyuan and the Anti-Smuggling Office requested a judgment ordering Yifa Company to compensate them for property losses; Su Xianggao and four others requested compensation for losses from the death of their relatives, moral damages, and personal property losses; Zhong Wu and 14 others requested compensation for personal property losses and moral suffering. The Guangzhou Maritime Court separated the claims into three cases based on the different causes of action. The first-instance judgment found: The "Yifa" vessel violated Article 37 of the Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China. At 0513 hours on November 25, 1992, it collided with the "Gongbian 001" vessel at 22°09'.9 N, 114°31'.5 E, causing "Gongbian 001" to sink. Yifa Company shall bear full liability for the personal injuries and property losses caused by the collision. Accordingly, the court entered separate judgments:

Ordering Yifa Company to pay Zhong Xiaoyuan RMB 2,390,400 and HKD 20,000; to pay the Anti-Smuggling Office RMB 226,420 and HKD 34,276; plus interest on each amount (calculated from February 23, 1993, to the date of payment, at the interest rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China for enterprise current demand deposits for the same period).

Ordering Yifa Company to pay compensation for the death losses of the relatives of Su Xianggao and Su Qirong, RMB 800,000 each; to pay compensation for the death loss of Li Xing's relative, RMB 384,000; to pay compensation for the death loss of Chen Hua's relative, RMB 435,896; to pay compensation for the death loss of Liu Yaoxiong's relative, RMB 531,200; and additionally, to pay RMB 1,000 to each deceased person's relative for the deceased's personal property loss.

Ordering Yifa Company to pay each of the survivors Zhong Wu, Zhong Jiarong, Zhong Jiazhong, Su Hua, Lu Zhihua, and Zhong Caibao RMB 10,000 for medical expenses and moral damages; to pay each of the survivors Zhong Muhuo, Su Zuwang, Su Wang, Xu Peng, Liu Guobao, Liang Fumin, Mao Xiangwu, and Cai Ji RMB 5,000 for moral damages; and additionally, to pay each survivor RMB 1,000 for personal property loss.

The litigation costs for the three cases were RMB 30,782, RMB 31,460, and RMB 7,043 respectively, all borne by Yifa Company.

After Yifa Company appealed, the Guangdong High People's Court, upon trial, held: The "Gongbian 001" vessel was a public service vessel performing official duties within China's maritime areas. Based on the observation data from the Observation Station, cross-referenced with the radar observation records of the Hong Kong Marine Department and the ship's log of the "Yifa" vessel, it could be determined that the vessel with serial number 847 at the Observation Station was the "Yifa" vessel. Based on the Observation Station's records and the testimony of the crew of "Gongbian 001," it could be determined that the vessel with serial number 036 at the Observation Station had a track essentially consistent with that of "Gongbian 001," and serial number 036 was the "Gongbian 001." The Observation Station records indicated that the "Yifa" vessel collided with "Gongbian 001" at 0513 hours at 22°09'.9 N, 114°31'.5 E, and "Gongbian 001" sank at 0520 hours. After the incident, the "Yifa" vessel continued eastward; its hull was black, its bridge was white, and it carried containers on deck, consistent with the description of the offending vessel provided by the crew of "Gongbian 001." The investigation by the Zhangjiagang Harbor Superintendency showed fresh scraping marks on the port side of the "Yifa" vessel, and the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau's paint test indicated that the paint extracted from the scraping marks on the "Yifa" vessel contained components identical to those in the paint of "Gongbian 001." The above evidence supported the finding that the "Yifa" vessel was the offending vessel. The positions of the sunken vessel and the rescued persons provided by Yifa Company were within less than 3 nautical miles of the position where the Observation Station observed the merging of echos and the disappearance of the echo. Due to the complexity of local currents, the evidence provided by Yifa Company was insufficient to overturn the conclusion reached in the first-instance judgment. Moreover, Yifa Company was unable to provide conclusive evidence that W500 was the "BARZAN" vessel. Therefore, Yifa Company's grounds for denying that the "Yifa" vessel was the offending vessel were insufficient, and its appellate claims were not supported. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law; the judgment ordering Yifa Company to bear liability for damages was correct. The court thus entered a final judgment: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed. The appellate litigation costs were borne by Yifa Company.

Yifa Company was dissatisfied with the final judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court and applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. The original judgment's findings of fact were unclear. (1) The opposing party provided false evidence to the court of first instance. The "observation and communication station's monitoring report" and testimony both stated that the Yifa vessel was the only eastbound merchant ship at that time, and that the "Yifa" vessel must have been the vessel responsible for the collision. This is inconsistent with the facts. There is ample evidence proving that at the time of the maritime incident, there was also a Qatari-flagged container vessel named "BARZAN" that was tracked by VTC and assigned code W500. This vessel departed Hong Kong heading eastbound toward Kaohsiung Port, and had collided with a small boat at sea at 0527 hours on November 25, 1992, at a location near the sunken vessel. (2) Yifa Company had already provided sufficient evidence to the court of first instance to prove that W500 on the VTC radar log was the "BARZAN" vessel. According to VTC tracking records, before 0426.6 hours on November 25, the "BARZAN" vessel was marked as "BAR01," and after 0428.6 hours, the code was changed to W500. The track lines of "BAR01" and W500 are continuous. If W500 were not the "BARZAN" vessel, then where did the "BARZAN" vessel go after 0426.6 hours? And where did W500 come from before 0428.6 hours? Furthermore, the "Marine Accident Report" of the master of the "BARZAN" vessel states that at 0527 hours on November 25, the vessel's position was consistent with the VTC record for W500 at 0527 hours. The original copy of the "Marine Accident Report" is kept at the Kaohsiung District Court and is a valid legal document notarized by that court. During the second trial hearing at first instance, the agent for the opposing party had to admit the authenticity of this document. The judgment of the original trial did not even mention this "Marine Accident Report." (3) Tidal movements always follow certain patterns. At that time and location, the tidal current was flowing to the southwest. The location of the "BARZAN" vessel's maritime incident was upstream of the sunken vessel and the location where the persons who fell overboard were rescued. However, the light spot merging position and the light spot disappearing position recorded by the observation and communication station were approximately 3 nautical miles downstream from the rescue location. A small boat with engine room flooding and persons who had fallen overboard could not possibly drift 3 nautical miles against the current. This is a very simple concept. The judgment of the original trial stated, "Due to the complexity of local sea currents, the evidence provided by the appellant is insufficient to overturn the conclusion reached in the first instance judgment." This finding violates science and is not based on facts. (4) The Anti-Smuggling Office of Zhuhai expropriated a fishing vessel for anti-smuggling operations, which is illegal. 2. The original judgment erred in its application of law. (1) The "Marine Accident Report" of the master of the "BARZAN" vessel was notarized through legal procedures, and the opposing party overturned this notarized fact without any evidence. The court of original trial's failure to admit it as evidence violates the provisions of Article 67 of Chapter VI of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. (2) It is legally impermissible for the original trial court to have admitted the "evidence" from the observation and communication station's "monitoring report" without obtaining the original copy or a true copy of that evidence. (3) The Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the PRC is administrative legislation concerning maritime traffic safety and does not contain provisions on how to apportion liability for vessel collisions and civil liability. China is a contracting party to the Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972. Whether the vessel "Shanwei 12138" was a fishing vessel or a government vessel, the collision dispute should be resolved by applying the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972, annexed to that Convention. The original trial court's failure to apply these Regulations and its decision to hold the "Yifa" vessel fully liable for the collision by applying the Maritime Traffic Safety Law constitute a serious error in the application of law.

The opposing party, Zhong Xiaoyuan, responded: 1. The data on the merging of two targets provided by the observation and communication station confirms that at the time of merging, W500 was still more than 1 nautical mile from our vessel. Moreover, the Hong Kong Marine Department never confirmed that W500 was the "BARZAN" vessel. The testimonies of the fishermen, the evidence obtained by Guangzhou Harbor Superintendency from the radar observation and communication station and provided by VTC, the evidence obtained during the investigation by Zhangjiagang Harbor Superintendency, the paint analysis report from the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau, and the investigation and analysis report on this maritime incident by the Guangzhou Harbor Superintendency Administration all prove that the "Yifa" vessel was the vessel responsible for the collision. The original trial's judgment that Yifa Company should bear civil liability is correct. 2. The "Marine Accident Report" notarized by the "affidavit" of the Kaohsiung District Court can only prove that the said "Marine Accident Report" was provided by that court. The "Marine Accident Report" does not contain a statement that the vessel "collided with a small boat." 3. The location where the US warship rescued the persons who fell overboard was 0.8 nautical miles in bearing from the position where the light spot disappeared. The claim of "drifting 3 nautical miles against the current" is unsupported by evidence.

The opposing party, the Anti-Smuggling Office, responded: 1. The Anti-Smuggling Office, in accordance with the directives and responsibilities of higher central authorities, summoned the vessel "Shanwei 12138" to participate in maritime anti-smuggling operations. During the anti-smuggling operation, the office dispatched anti-smuggling personnel to command, and the vessel's name was changed to "Gongbian 001." This fully complies with the working principles and functions of the Anti-Smuggling Office. The anti-smuggling vessel "Gongbian 001" was a government vessel performing official duties within China's territorial waters. There is absolutely no basis for the claim of illegally expropriating a fishing vessel for anti-smuggling purposes. 2. Numerous pieces of evidence in this case prove that the vessel responsible for colliding with and sinking the "Gongbian 001," which was performing official duties, is the "Yifa" vessel. The evidence is conclusive. Yifa Company's denial of the fact that it collided with and sank the "Gongbian 001" vessel is intended to evade legal liability and punishment. 3. In order to evade legal liability, Yifa Company falsely claimed that the Hong Kong Marine Department confirmed that W500 was the "BARZAN" vessel, and deliberately mistranslated the "BARZAN" vessel's maritime declaration. The Hong Kong Marine Department has never issued any document proving that W500 was the "BARZAN" vessel. 4. The vessel "Gongbian 001" was intentionally rammed and sunk by the "Yifa" vessel while performing official duties. The "Gongbian 001" vessel was not at fault in any way. The "Yifa" vessel fled the scene without regard for the safety of human lives on the other vessel, resulting in the serious incident of six deaths. This incident cannot be understood as an ordinary vessel collision accident, and liability for the collision should not be apportioned according to ordinary vessel collision rules.

The opposing parties, Su Xianggao, Zhong Wu, and 17 others, responded: 1. Among the persons rescued from the water that day, Zhong Wu, Mai Yong, and Liang Fumin, when questioned by the Hong Kong Marine Police and the master of the "STARLING," stated that the vessel was collided with at approximately 0510 hours and sank approximately 10 minutes after the collision. The three individuals gave their statements regarding the times of the collision and sinking at different times and in different places. Their testimonies were given immediately after being rescued, constitute first-hand information in this case, and are also important evidence. 2. Considering all other evidence in this case, only the "Yifa" vessel meets all the conditions that the vessel which collided with and sank the "Gongbian 001" must satisfy. 3. Yifa Company's claims that W500 was the "BARZAN" vessel, that the master of the "BARZAN" vessel stated he collided with a small boat, and concerning the current at that time and place have all been refused recognition by the courts of first instance and second instance based on legal reasoning. In summary, it is fully proven that the vessel responsible for the collision is the "Yifa" vessel.

The Supreme People's Court, upon retrial, opines as follows:

The evidence in this case concerning the collision between the vessel "Shanwei 12138" and the "Yifa" vessel is all circumstantial evidence. Circumstantial evidence can only be used as a basis for determining facts if it can corroborate each other; contradictory circumstantial evidence cannot be so used.

The tidal current certificate issued by the South China Sea Marine Information Center of the State Oceanic Administration concerning the sea area where the maritime incident occurred on November 25, 1992, corroborates evidence including Chinese and English charts, tidal data, and the testimony of the master of the British Navy vessel "PEACOCK." This tidal current certificate is scientific and objective. None of the parties have ever raised any objection to this evidence, and it shall be admitted. The reference in the final judgment of the original trial to "local complexity of sea currents" lacks a basis for determination.

The US Navy vessel "STARLING" was the rescuer. Its report stating the position where the persons who fell overboard were rescued as 22°09'.3 North latitude, 114°33'.1 East longitude is primary, original evidence. The US vessel rescued 15 persons who had fallen overboard within approximately 25 minutes, indicating that the persons who fell overboard were not far apart. This is consistent with the testimony of the armed police soldiers who fell overboard. The final judgment of the original trial correctly determined the position where the persons who fell overboard were rescued. According to the testimony of the master of the British Navy vessel "PEACOCK," which participated in the search and rescue, that vessel's method of searching for the newly sunken vessel was scientific and objective. No other vessel had sunk in that waters on that day or before the occurrence of this maritime incident. Therefore, it can be determined that the sunken vessel identified by the master of the "PEACOCK" at 22°09'.4 North latitude, 114°34'.1 East longitude is the vessel "Shanwei 12138."

The on-site inspection record made by Zhangjiagang Harbor Superintendency of the "Yifa" vessel and the photographs taken of the "Yifa" vessel are objective and timely. None of the parties have ever raised any objection to the probative force of this inspection record or these photographs, and they shall be used as evidence. According to the "Marine Accident Report" of the "Shanwei 12138" vessel and the statements of the fishermen, the port side of the bow of the vessel responsible for the collision struck the port side engine room compartment of the "Shanwei 12138," causing the engine room to flood and the vessel to sink rapidly. Expert analysis indicates that obvious collision marks should have remained on the port side of the bow of the vessel responsible for the collision. However, from the photographs and the inspection record, it can be seen that there were no scraping marks on the bow (port side) of the "Yifa" vessel, and certainly no obvious dents or hull damage. The opposing parties also admitted at the time of the on-site inspection that there were no collision marks on the bow of the "Yifa" vessel. This fact shall be recognized. The paint scrapings on the midship section and aft of the "Yifa" vessel are insufficient to constitute marks indicating a collision that caused the steel-hulled fishing vessel "Shanwei 12138" to sink.

In the paint inspection report conducted by the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau on the paint film taken from the "Yifa" vessel, some corresponding peak values differed by more than 50 wave numbers. The conclusion of the inspection report was that the paint "contained the same components as the paint in the control sample," not that the components were identical. This inspection result cannot prove that the non-original paint found on the damaged paint areas of the "Yifa" vessel was the paint from the "Shanwei 12138" vessel.

In the "monitoring report" from the observation and communication station, the track of the light spot in batch No. 036 from merging to disappearance does not match the course and speed of the "Shanwei 12138" vessel after the collision, as stated by the fishermen. The "Shanwei 12138" vessel was at sea for over 9 hours on this voyage and only measured one ship's position (an approximate position) at around 0500 hours. There is no accurate record of the time and changes in course and speed. The observation and communication station's selection of light spots from among the numerous fishing vessel light spots on the radar screen was highly arbitrary and cannot prove objective facts. The judgment of the original trial improperly determined that the track of the light spot in batch No. 036 was generally consistent with the track of the "Shanwei 12138" vessel. The tracking record provided by the Hong Kong Marine Department indicates that the vessel with code W500 passed near the so-called batch 036 light spot merging position and light spot disappearing position at 0517 hours and 0520 hours respectively, heading eastbound, at a distance of less than 1 cable. The "monitoring report" shows that from 0100 to 0732 hours on the day of the maritime incident, only one foreign merchant vessel departed Hong Kong heading eastbound. This contradicts evidence including the departure information for the "BARZAN" vessel from the Hong Kong Marine Department, the VTC tracking record, and the "BARZAN" vessel's marine accident report. The "monitoring report's" account of the relevant vessel dynamics at the time and place of the collision is clearly inconsistent with objective facts. The "monitoring report" is not an original record, nor was it verified against the original record according to law. In summary, this "monitoring report" contains internal contradictions in reflecting the facts of the vessel collision, contradicts other evidence, and lacks authenticity and objectivity. It shall not be admitted.

Considering comprehensively the following objective facts: the bow of the "Yifa" vessel had no collision marks or damage; the paint adhering to the port side of the "Yifa" vessel was not identical to the paint of the "Shanwei 12138" vessel; the "Yifa" vessel did not make a significant left turn or reduce speed when passing through the incident area; the relative situation of the collision position claimed by the opposing parties and the position of the sunken vessel and the rescue location of the persons who fell overboard did not conform to the tidal current at that time and place; and there was a container vessel that departed Hong Kong and passed through the incident area heading eastbound at the time of the maritime incident, the evidence is insufficient to determine that the "Yifa" vessel was the vessel responsible for the collision. The original trial’s judgment that the “Yifa” vessel was the vessel responsible for the collision constitutes an error in fact-finding and shall be corrected.

The claims made by the opposing parties in their responses that the vessel responsible for the collision departed Hong Kong via the east fairway of Po Liu before 0300 hours on that day, and that the fishing vessel “Shanwei 12138” did not stop after the collision, are not supported by evidence and are not recognized.

The opposing parties bear the burden of proof for their claim that the “Yifa” vessel was the vessel that collided with and sank the “Shanwei 12138.” If they cannot provide sufficient evidence to support their claim, their claims will not be supported. The original trial judgment’s findings of fact were unclear, its application of law was erroneous, and its decision ordering the retrial applicant, Yifa Company, to bear the losses of property and personal injury caused by the collision involving the fishing vessel “Shanwei 12138” was an improper judgment that shall be corrected.

In conclusion, the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the provisions of Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered separate judgments on May 18, 1999:

1. Set aside the three second-instance civil judgments of the Guangdong High People's Court in this case;
2. Set aside the three first-instance civil judgments of the Guangzhou Maritime Court in this case;
3. Dismiss the claims of the opposing parties, Zhong Xiaoyuan and the Zhuhai Anti-Smuggling Office;
4. Dismiss the claims of the opposing parties, Su Xianggao, Su Qirong, Li Xing, Chen Hua, Liu Yaoxiong, and others;
5. Dismiss the claims of the opposing parties, Zhong Wu, Zhong Muhuo, Su Zuwang, Su Wang, Su Hua, Xu Peng, Zhong Caibao, Zhong Jiarong, Zhong Jiazhong, Lu Zhihua, Cai Ji, Liu Guobao, Liang Fumin, Mao Xiangwu, and others.

The litigation costs for the first and second instances shall be borne by the opposing parties in each respective case. However, in consideration of the deaths of the relatives of Su Xianggao, Su Qirong, Li Xing, Chen Hua, Liu Yaoxiong, and others in this maritime incident, and their family financial difficulties, the costs are waived. The second-instance litigation costs that should be borne by the 14 individuals, including Zhong Wu, Zhong Muhuo, Su Zuwang, Su Wang, Su Hua, Xu Peng, Zhong Caibao, Zhong Jiarong, Zhong Jiazhong, Lu Zhihua, Cai Ji, Liu Guobao, Liang Fumin, and Mao Xiangwu, are hereby excused.
